Guard against adjusting for a covariate downstream of treatment

Source: R/guards.R
pollin_guard_posttreatment.Rd

Adjusting a treatment contrast for a variable the treatment itself changes (for example vegetative weight, or a pollinator visit count under a cage) blocks part of the effect and can open a collider path. Whether a covariate is downstream of treatment is a fact about the system that the data cannot reveal. The declaration is the user's: downstream names the variables the user holds to be affected by treatment, and the guard stops if any adjustment covariate in x is among them.

Usage

pollin_guard_posttreatment(x, downstream)

Arguments

x

A pollin_data(), pollin_design() or pollin_estimand() object.

downstream

Character vector of variables declared downstream of treatment. character(0) declares none. There is no default.

Value

x, invisibly, when no adjustment covariate is declared downstream.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  pods = rpois(40, 30),
  trt = rep(c("Cage", "Open"), 20),
  Site = rep(letters[1:4], each = 10),
  rain = rep(c(250, 300, 320, 410), each = 10),
  veg_weight = rnorm(40, 100, 10)
)
pd <- pollin_data(df, "pods", "trt", unit = "Site", adjust = "rain")
pollin_guard_posttreatment(pd, downstream = "veg_weight")

pd2 <- pollin_data(df, "pods", "trt", unit = "Site",
                   adjust = c("rain", "veg_weight"))
try(pollin_guard_posttreatment(pd2, downstream = "veg_weight"))
#> Error : Adjustment covariate `veg_weight` is declared downstream of `trt`. Adjusting for a downstream covariate removes part of the treatment effect; drop it from `adjust`.
